pairs.question: Quare autem rotunda sit grando?
pairs.answer: Etiam sine magistro scire possis, cum adnotaueris stillicidium omne glomerari, quod et in speculis apparet, quae umorem halitu colligunt, et in poculis sparsis aliaque omni leuitate; non minus foliis si quae guttae adhaeserunt, in rotundum iacent.
pairs.derivation: Authorial self-posed question 'quare autem rotunda sit grando' (why hail is round) immediately answered by the author himself. The original is one continuous sentence; I split it at the implicit question mark after 'grando'. Question normalized: capitalized first word, terminal '?'. Answer is the contiguous remainder of the same sentence (from 'etiam sine magistro...' to the first/only full stop at 'in rotundum iacent.'), explaining that every drop forms into a ball; first word capitalized. Nothing was cut from the middle; the next section [3,4] begins a new topic (the poetic quotations on water carving stone).
